method: Official vendor values are preferred. A slash in NVIDIA material is dense/sparse unless the footnote says otherwise. status=derived means arithmetic from an official peak using an architecture-documented ratio; it is not a benchmark.

rentalPricing.statistic: simple unweighted arithmetic mean of the listed public per-GPU hourly samples
rentalPricing.caveat: not volume-weighted; community, secure, and on-demand tiers are labeled in rentalSamples; spot and reserved are excluded unless explicitly stated

gpus.name: NVIDIA H20 SXM 96GB

gpus.name: NVIDIA H800 PCIe 80GB
gpus.notes: The NVIDIA-authored 2023 product brief marks the headline Tensor figures as structurally sparse; dense values are its official values divided by two. NVIDIA vGPU documentation confirms the PCIe 80GB board and MIG profiles. The 2023-03-21 date is the first public shipment confirmation, not a formal NVIDIA newsroom launch date. No public MSRP or current public USD rental quote was found.

gpus.name: NVIDIA H800 SXM5 80GB
gpus.notes: H800 SXM preserves H100-class low-precision Tensor throughput and 3.35TB/s HBM bandwidth, while FP64 and NVLink are restricted. The NVIDIA-authored 2023 product brief supplies the sparse values; dense values are those official figures divided by two. The 2023-03-21 date is the first public shipment confirmation, not a formal NVIDIA newsroom launch date.

gpus.name: NVIDIA B300 SXM
gpus.notes: Official HGX values are for an 8-GPU baseboard. Per-GPU values divide the system totals by eight; the official footnote marks INT8 as sparse, so 3 POPS system sparse becomes 375 TOPS sparse and 187.5 TOPS dense per GPU. FP4 is official sparse|dense divided by eight.

gpus.name: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition
gpus.notes: Official product page provides FP4/FP8/FP16/BF16 but does not label sparsity inline; values align with sparse FP4=4P and dense FP8=1P architecture ratio. Rental labels may mix server/workstation edition.
